You're hard on yourself in ways you'd never be with a friend.

blocks.faith.heading: Faith at the center, never forced
blocks.faith.body:
CBT asks: is this thought true? For many Christians that fits naturally, including what you believe about God and about yourself. If you want it, your counselor can bring Scripture into that work, weighing your thoughts against what's true.

If you'd rather leave faith out, your counselor's care is just as thorough, and they follow your lead. [How faith works at Freedom](/christian-counseling)

sections.body: Cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT) is a practical, structured kind of counseling that helps you change the thoughts and habits that keep a problem going, so you can feel and live differently. It's one of the most researched forms of therapy there is. CBT was developed by psychiatrist Aaron Beck in the 1960s.
sections.heading: What is cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT)?

sections.body: CBT is built on a simple idea: how you think, how you feel, and what you do all affect each other. When thoughts get stuck in unhelpful patterns, feelings and actions follow. CBT helps you spot those patterns, test them against what's actually true, and try new responses. It's one of the most widely researched forms of counseling, with strong evidence for anxiety, depression, and stress.
sections.heading: How thoughts, feelings, and actions connect

sections.body: You and your counselor set clear goals together. Sessions often include learning a skill, practicing it, and choosing something small to try before next time. Many people find CBT helpful because they can see progress.
sections.heading: Structured, collaborative, and goal-focused
How CBT works
sections.body:
1. You and your counselor pick specific goals.
2. You learn to notice the thoughts that show up in hard moments, and to test whether they're accurate or helpful.
3. You try small changes in what you do, and see what happens.
4. You practice between sessions, because the skills grow with use.

sections.heading: What CBT helps with
sections.body: [Anxiety](/anxiety-depression-counseling) and worry, panic, [depression](/depression-counseling), low self-esteem, perfectionism, ADHD in [children and teens](/child-teen-counseling), and unhelpful habits.

sections.heading: How long CBT takes
sections.body: It varies, but CBT is usually shorter-term than open-ended talk therapy: many people work through a focused course over a few months, then spread sessions out.

sections.heading: Honest limits
sections.body: CBT is active: it works best when you practice between sessions. It focuses on the present more than the past, so if old hurts keep driving today's reactions, your counselor may pair it with approaches like [internal family systems (IFS)](/ifs-therapy) or [EMDR](/trauma-emdr-counseling).

sections.heading: CBT or ACT?
sections.body: Both are practical. CBT helps you change unhelpful thoughts; [acceptance and commitment therapy (ACT)](/act-therapy) helps you stop fighting them and move toward what matters. Many people benefit from both, and our counselors often combine them.

blocks.expect.heading: Your first session
blocks.expect.body: Your first session is about understanding what's been hard and what you'd like to change, so you and your counselor can set goals together. Sessions are in our Middletown office or online.
blocks.cost.body: We don't bill insurance, but you can pay with an HSA or FSA card, and we'll give you a superbill to submit for possible out-of-network reimbursement.
